comparison: Both evaluate claims C18-C23, C73-C74 about the in vitro model establishment and find them SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative validation with statistical tests, while peer reviewers (all three) affirm the model's validity and utility. Peer review includes C75 (model summary) which OpenEval addresses separately in R13.

Perfect agreement on claims C24-C27 regarding differential regenerative capacity between axon types. Both find these claims SUPPORTED with strong experimental evidence from laser axotomy experiments. Reviewers 1 and 2 explicitly endorse these findings as important observations.

OpenEval evaluates C28-C32 (microtubule dynamics and mitochondrial transport) as SUPPORTED, while peer review R3 only addresses C28 (mitochondrial transport asymmetry) as SUPPORTED. Peer review R4 covers the remaining microtubule dynamics claims (C29-C32) that OpenEval groups together.

Partial overlap: OpenEval R3 covers C28-C32 while peer R4 covers C4, C29-C32. Both find microtubule dynamics differences (C29-C32) SUPPORTED. Peer review explicitly connects these to spastin levels and notes findings are 'clearly shown.'

OpenEval evaluates in vivo validation claims C33-C36 as SUPPORTED, while peer R5 addresses C5, C33-C36. Both find the in vivo microtubule dynamics data SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers particularly value the in vivo validation as strengthening the in vitro findings.

Perfect agreement on claims C6, C37-C40 regarding conditioning lesion effects on microtubule dynamics. Both find these SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers emphasize this as an 'important' finding showing loss of MAP asymmetry after conditioning.

Perfect agreement on claims C7, C41-C44 about MAP distribution differences. Both find these SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers highlight the identification of molecular signatures as a strength that advances understanding of regenerative capacity differences.

Perfect agreement on claims C8, C45-C46 regarding conditioning lesion effects on MAPs and persistent tau asymmetry. Both find these SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept the findings without challenge, though OpenEval notes the tau interpretation is somewhat speculative.

Perfect agreement on claims C47-C48 about mRNA distribution. Both find these SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this is a negative result that doesn't rule out other mechanisms; peer reviewers accept without specific comment.

Perfect agreement on claims C49-C50 regarding EB3 comet behavior at T-junction. Both find these SUPPORTED as part of the microtubule dynamics characterization showing significant differences between branches.
Perfect agreement on claim C51 about δ2 tubulin enrichment in peripheral-like axons. Both find this SUPPORTED as part of the MAP signature characterization that differentiates axon types.

Perfect agreement on claims C9, C52-C54 regarding spastin knockout effects on microtubule dynamics. Both find these SUPPORTED. Peer Reviewer 3 explicitly highlights this as a strength demonstrating causal relationships.

Strong disagreement on claims C10, C55-C58, C60 regarding spastin knockout effects on regeneration. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED, but peer review rates them UNCERTAIN. Reviewer 3 critiques Figure 5H-J methodology (needs astrocyte markers, CTB tracing concerns) and notes the study lacks convincing mechanistic insights. Reviewer 1 acknowledges this only 'partially addresses' causal link concerns.

Significant disagreement on claims C75-C77 (model validation summary). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED by comprehensive data, but peer review rates them UNCERTAIN. Reviewer 3 questions the model's validity, requests further characterization of branch classification, and suggests need for 3D models and more physiologically relevant substrates. Reviewers 1-2 are more positive about model utility.

Disagreement on claims C78-C79 linking δ2 tubulin to mitochondrial sorting. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN noting the causal link is speculative and not directly tested. Peer review rates SUPPORTED, accepting the mechanistic interpretation without challenge, though it remains speculative.

Disagreement on claim C67 about microtubule stabilization after conditioning lesion. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting direct evidence for increased stability is not provided. Peer review rates SUPPORTED, accepting the inference without challenge as aligning with conditioning lesion effects.

OpenEval evaluates background/context claims C1-C3, C11-C17 as SUPPORTED by cited literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers focus on novel findings rather than cataloging background claims.

OpenEval evaluates background/mechanistic context claims C61-C72, C80 as SUPPORTED by cited literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these represent contextual knowledge rather than novel experimental findings.

OpenEval evaluates core summary claims C4-C5, C59 as SUPPORTED, noting they are covered in detail elsewhere. These overlap partially with peer R4 (C4), R5 (C5), and R13 (C59), but no single peer result addresses this specific grouping as a summary statement.
